The fact that the script sometimes reproduces the issue and some times not is likely due to [hash randomization](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__hash__) of the python interpreter.
Using a PYTHONHASHSEED=0 makes the script always succeed; using PYTHONHASHSEED=1 makes it always fail:
```
$ PYTHONHASHSEED=1 python test_bug.py

```
im not sure COLLATE works on mariadb at all.  trying mysql
also, please confirm you are using either python 2 or an older 3.x version , I think preceding 3.6.  can't reproduce on 3.7

here's the patch, ENGINE does not seem to matter
```

diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
index d009d656e..d219918fc 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/mysql/base.py
@@ -1697,6 +1697,8 @@ class MySQLDDLCompiler(compiler.DDLCompiler):
             [
                 ("DEFAULT_CHARSET", "COLLATE"),
                 ("DEFAULT_CHARACTER_SET", "COLLATE"),
+                ("CHARSET", "COLLATE"),
+                ("CHARACTER_SET", "COLLATE"),
             ],
             nonpart_options,
         ):

```

needs PR w/ tests or someone will get to it

It does look like CI fiddles with PYTHONHASHSEED before starting the tests:

``` text
py38-cext-sqlite-postgresql run-test-pre: PYTHONHASHSEED='2491140407'
```

I guess we'll have to see if the tests for this particular issue require a specific value in order to pass or fail consistently.

**Gord Thompson** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Fix mysql CREATE TABLE / COLLATE issue** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2133

**Gord Thompson** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Fix mysql CREATE TABLE / COLLATE issue** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2134

Okay, not sure how far down the rabbit hole we want to go with this. My original test — shamelessly cribbed from the repro code above — actually tested that the table was created with the proper collation, not whether the trailing options were rendered in the exact same order every time. That's not particularly important; what *is* important is that the `COLLATE` option appears last:

``` none
mysql> SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'collation_database';
+--------------------+--------------------+
| Variable_name      | Value              |
+--------------------+--------------------+
| collation_database | utf8mb4_general_ci |
+--------------------+--------------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> CREATE TABLE test_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY) COLLATE utf8_icelandic_ci ENGINE=InnoDB CHARSET=utf8;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.14 sec)

mysql> select TABLE_COLLATION, ENGINE from information_schema.TABLES where table_name = 'test_table';
+-----------------+--------+
| TABLE_COLLATION | ENGINE |
+-----------------+--------+
| utf8_general_ci | InnoDB |
+-----------------+--------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)

mysql> DROP TABLE test_table;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.04 sec)

mysql> CREATE TABLE test_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY) ENGINE=InnoDB CHARSET=utf8 COLLATE utf8_icelandic_ci;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)

mysql> select TABLE_COLLATION, ENGINE from information_schema.TABLES where table_name = 'test_table';
+-------------------+--------+
| TABLE_COLLATION   | ENGINE |
+-------------------+--------+
| utf8_icelandic_ci | InnoDB |
+-------------------+--------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> DROP TABLE test_table;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.04 sec)

mysql> CREATE TABLE test_table (id INT PRIMARY KEY) CHARSET=utf8 ENGINE=InnoDB COLLATE utf8_icelandic_ci;
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)

mysql> select TABLE_COLLATION, ENGINE from information_schema.TABLES where table_name = 'test_table';
+-------------------+--------+
| TABLE_COLLATION   | ENGINE |
+-------------------+--------+
| utf8_icelandic_ci | InnoDB |
+-------------------+--------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```

The current test code fails because sometimes the DDL is rendered as ENGINE/CHARSET/COLLATE and other times it is rendered as CHARSET/ENGINE/COLLATE, but both of those are "correct" in terms of their ultimate effect.
you can always add another dependency tuple like I did above just to get the test to work.

Tried that, but simply adding `("ENGINE", "COLLATE"),` was insufficient, and adding 4 more for `("ENGINE", "CHARSET"),` et al. seemed to be unnecessarily tedious. I just modified the test to check for both variations.
mariadb at least seems to actually ignore the collate if the order is wrong.  no error or nothing.   wow

issue.title: Intermittent "test_update_to_expression_two" failures

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

issue.body:
My first patchset for [Gerrit 2143](https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2143) had a single failure in

[sqlalchemy_gerrit/cext=cext,db=mysql,pyv=py27](https://jenkins.sqlalchemy.org/job/sqlalchemy_gerrit/cext=cext,db=mysql,pyv=py27/5459/)

specifically [this](https://jenkins.sqlalchemy.org/job/sqlalchemy_gerrit/cext=cext,db=mysql,pyv=py27/5459/testReport/junit/test.sql.test_update/UpdateTest/test_update_to_expression_two/):

``` none
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/jenkins/workspace/sqlalchemy_gerrit/20384d2e/test/sql/test_update.py", line 886, in test_update_to_expression_two
    checkpositional=(5, 7, 10, 18),
  File "/home/jenkins/workspace/sqlalchemy_gerrit/20384d2e/.tox/py27-cext-mysql/lib/python2.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/testing/assertions.py", line 439, in assert_compile
    eq_(cc, result, "%r != %r on dialect %r" % (cc, result, dialect))
  File "/home/jenkins/workspace/sqlalchemy_gerrit/20384d2e/.tox/py27-cext-mysql/lib/python2.7/site-packages/sqlalchemy/testing/assertions.py", line 207, in eq_
    assert a == b, msg or "%r != %r" % (a, b)
AssertionError: u'UPDATE foo SET data2[?]=?, data1[?]=?' != 'UPDATE foo SET data1[?]=?, data2[?]=?' on dialect <sqlalchemy.engine.default.StrCompileDialect object at 0x7f35acce5c10>
assert 'UPDATE foo S...?, data1[?]=?' == 'UPDATE foo SE...?, data2[?]=?'
  - UPDATE foo SET data2[?]=?, data1[?]=?
  + UPDATE foo SET data1[?]=?, data2[?]=?
```

I seemed to recall having seen a failure like that before, so I did a `recheck` and CI failed again, but this time it wasn't "db=mysql,pyv=py27" that failed, it was

[sqlalchemy_gerrit/cext=nocext,db=sqlite-postgresql,pyv=py27](https://jenkins.sqlalchemy.org/job/sqlalchemy_gerrit/cext=nocext,db=sqlite-postgresql,pyv=py27/5460/)

Same test failing, both py27, but the first time it was mysql that failed and postgresql that passed, while on `recheck` it was the other way around.

I wonder if this is somehow similar to the recent behaviour seen in #5411 where "the order of things" can be non-deterministic based on [hash randomization](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/5411#issuecomment-646969210)?

body:
>mariadb at least seems to actually ignore the collate if the order is wrong. no error or nothing. wow

Yes, I've just run into this behavior. MariaDB will ignore the collation if it doesn't appear last and then pickup the default from the SCHEMA -- ignoring the explicitly provided one if it comes prior to a CHARSET.

For future searchers: this can then break FKs to string fields with further cryptic 105 errors that were difficult to debug in production and pipelines.

For example, the SQL emitted from Alembic migration CreateTable() that reads:
```COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci CHARSET=utf8mb4 ENGINE=InnoDB``` would in my case cause the columns to pick up utf8mb4_general_ci (SCHEMA default) which would then fail on FK creation with mismatched FK definitions.
